quests.question: The train ___ the city centre every fifteen minutes.
quests.hint: One train is singular - the verb needs -s or -es.
quests.explanation: 'The train' is singular, so the verb must be 'passes'. Verbs ending in -ss, -sh, -ch, -x, or -o add -es, not just -s.

quests.question: Express trains ___ the city centre without stopping.
quests.hint: 'Express trains' is plural - use the base form.
quests.explanation: 'Express trains' is plural, so the verb is 'pass'. The base form is used for all plural subjects in the simple present.

quests.question: My neighbour ___ her garden every weekend.
quests.hint: One neighbour is singular - the verb needs -s.
quests.explanation: 'My neighbour' is singular (one person), so the verb takes -s: 'waters'. This is the standard rule for all singular third-person subjects.

quests.question: The museum ___ free admission on Sundays.
quests.hint: One museum is singular - add -s or -es to the verb.
quests.explanation: 'The museum' is singular, so the verb is 'offers'. The -s ending signals agreement with a third-person singular subject.

quests.question: Several museums in this city ___ free admission on Sundays.
quests.hint: Multiple museums is a plural subject - use the base form.
quests.explanation: 'Several museums' is plural, so the verb stays as 'offer'. 'Several' signals a plural noun, and plural nouns take the base verb form.

quests.question: It ___ about twenty minutes to walk to the station.
quests.hint: 'It' is always singular - add -s to the verb.
quests.explanation: The pronoun 'it' is always third-person singular, so the verb takes -s: 'it takes'. This applies even in expressions of time and distance.

quests.question: The company ___ its staff a bonus every December.
quests.hint: One company is singular - the verb needs -s.
quests.explanation: 'The company' is singular, so the verb must be 'gives'. In subject-verb agreement, singular subjects take a verb with -s in the simple present.

quests.question: Both companies ___ their staff a bonus every December.
quests.hint: 'Both companies' is plural - use the base form.
quests.explanation: 'Both companies' is plural, so the verb is 'give'. 'Both' always introduces a plural subject, which takes the base verb form.

quests.question: The toddler ___ all her vegetables at dinner.
quests.hint: One toddler is singular - add -s to the verb.
quests.explanation: 'The toddler' is a singular noun, so the verb takes -s: 'eats'. The -s ending is the mark of third-person singular agreement.

quests.question: This laptop ___ out of battery very quickly.
quests.hint: One laptop is singular - the verb needs -s.
quests.explanation: 'This laptop' is singular, so the verb must be 'runs'. Singular nouns and pronouns in third person always take a verb with -s.

quests.question: These laptops ___ out of battery very quickly.
quests.hint: 'These laptops' is plural - use the base form.
quests.explanation: 'These laptops' is plural, so the verb stays as 'run'. No -s is added to verbs when the subject is plural.

quests.question: The baker ___ fresh croissants early every morning.
quests.hint: One baker is singular - add -s or -es to the verb.
quests.explanation: 'The baker' is a singular noun, so the verb is 'makes'. The -s ending on the verb always signals a singular third-person subject.

quests.question: My son ___ football for his school team.
quests.hint: One person ('my son') is singular - the verb needs -s.
quests.explanation: 'My son' is singular (one person), so the verb takes -s: 'plays'. This is the fundamental subject-verb agreement rule in the simple present.

quests.question: My sons ___ football for different school teams.
quests.hint: More than one son is plural - use the base form.
quests.explanation: 'My sons' is plural, so the verb is 'play'. When the subject is plural, the verb takes its base form with no -s ending.

quests.question: The hotel ___ a complimentary breakfast to all guests.
quests.hint: One hotel is singular - add -s or -es to the verb.
quests.explanation: 'The hotel' is singular, so the verb is 'provides'. Any single noun in third person requires the verb to have an -s ending.

quests.question: She ___ yoga three times a week.
quests.hint: Pronouns like 'she' always take a verb with -s in the simple present.
quests.explanation: 'She' is a third-person singular pronoun, so 'practises' is correct. The -s ending on the verb shows agreement with he, she, or it.

quests.question: They ___ yoga together every Saturday morning.
quests.hint: Plural pronouns like 'they' never add -s to the verb.
quests.explanation: 'They' is always plural, so the verb must be 'practise'. Whenever the subject is 'we', 'you', or 'they', the verb takes its base form.

quests.question: The library ___ an enormous collection of rare books.
quests.hint: One library is singular - the verb needs -s.
quests.explanation: 'The library' is singular, so the verb must be 'holds'. Third-person singular subjects always require a verb with an -s ending.

quests.question: The doctor ___ her patients for thirty minutes each.
quests.hint: A single doctor is one person - singular verbs end in -s.
quests.explanation: 'The doctor' is a singular noun, so the verb is 'sees'. Adding -s to the verb marks it as third-person singular.

quests.question: The doctors at this clinic ___ patients all day.
quests.hint: Multiple doctors is a plural subject - use the base form.
quests.explanation: 'The doctors' is plural, so the verb is 'see'. When the subject is plural, the verb takes its base form without -s.

quests.question: This song ___ on the radio every single morning.
quests.hint: One song is singular - add -s to the verb.
quests.explanation: 'This song' is singular (one thing), so the verb takes -s: 'plays'. Singular subjects in third person always need a verb with -s.

quests.question: The football team ___ its home matches on Saturdays.
quests.hint: One team is singular - the verb needs -s.
quests.explanation: 'The football team' is singular as a unit, so the verb is 'plays'. In American and standard English, team names take singular verbs.

quests.question: The players ___ their home matches on Saturdays.
quests.hint: 'The players' is plural - use the base form.
quests.explanation: 'The players' is plural (many individuals), so the verb is 'play'. When we refer to the individuals rather than the team as a unit, the plural verb is used.

quests.question: My cousin ___ for a major airline.
quests.hint: One cousin is singular - add -s to the verb.
quests.explanation: 'My cousin' is singular (one person), so the verb takes -s: 'works'. Any singular noun in third person requires the -s ending on the verb.

quests.question: The package ___ two to three days to arrive.
quests.hint: One package is singular - the verb needs -s.
quests.explanation: 'The package' is singular, so the verb is 'takes'. Third-person singular subjects in simple present always require a verb with -s.

quests.question: International packages ___ longer to arrive than local ones.
quests.hint: 'International packages' is plural - use the base form.
quests.explanation: 'International packages' is plural, so the verb is 'take'. The base form is always used for plural subjects in simple present.

quests.question: The receptionist ___ all incoming calls before noon.
quests.hint: One receptionist is singular - add -s or -es to the verb.
quests.explanation: 'The receptionist' is singular, so the verb must be 'answers'. Verbs ending in -er, -en, or -s just add -s to form the third-person singular.

quests.question: Every customer ___ a free sample at the door.
quests.hint: 'Every customer' is treated as singular - the verb needs -s.
quests.explanation: 'Every' always makes the noun singular, even though it refers to many people. So 'every customer receives' is correct, not 'receive'.

quests.question: The customers ___ a free sample at the door.
quests.hint: 'The customers' is plural - use the base form.
quests.explanation: 'The customers' is plural, so the verb is 'receive'. The -s ending on 'receives' is only for singular subjects.

quests.question: She ___ the children to school every morning.
quests.hint: 'She' is singular - add -s to the verb.
quests.explanation: The pronoun 'she' is always third-person singular, so the verb takes -s: 'drives'. This is the core rule for he, she, and it.
